text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwean womens' organisations, worried about loopholes in the Administration of Estates Amendment Bill now before parliament, will meet female members of parliament on Monday to see if these loopholes can be closed as the bill goes through the house.

- Zimbabwe's higher education ministry has put in place measures to control the increasing number of unregistered private colleges which charge exhorbitant fees and award certificates not recognised by the government or the private sector.

- The government will soon establish a road fund to raise more than $800 million needed this year to maintain the country's road network, secretary for transport and energy Paul Kodzwa said last week.
